data.body: Prior-ticket constraints and maintained-OSS survey (recorded here as the AC evidence artifact). cinderlike-weariful-angora requires a real loopback Git protocol server, upload-pack filter support inherited through a temporary global config, packet-trace proof of filter negotiation, a known missing historical blob, an incompressible historical object larger than 140 MiB for the pack guard, and yield/finally terminate-wait-kill cleanup; configuration inspection or mocks are insufficient. Maintained-project status was checked on 2026-08-15: git/git, jelmer/dulwich, and eclipse-jgit/jgit were unarchived and had pushes on 2026-08-15, 2026-08-15, and 2026-08-14 respectively. Evidence: Git's t/lib-git-daemon.sh at https://github.com/git/git/blob/f43d01ab90be2711927c8d265b3fb21d2213d2ab/t/lib-git-daemon.sh owns one loopback daemon per test script and registers stop_git_daemon at exit; t/test-lib-functions.sh at https://github.com/git/git/blob/a592d6feb3d47a1fcd6be5b4c8136e116c26ffbc/t/test-lib-functions.sh derives distinct ports for parallel stress jobs. Dulwich's partial-clone compatibility suite at https://github.com/jelmer/dulwich/blob/88dfdb60f2e6fd4aeb658cd369b361397af1fb36/tests/compat/test_partial_clone.py uses small blobs, an ephemeral TCPGitServer on port 0, per-test temporary repositories, and registered shutdown/server-close/thread-join cleanup while exercising real git clone filters. JGit's daemon tests at https://github.com/eclipse-jgit/jgit/blob/5c5f7c6b146b24f2bd4afae1902df85ad6e57ea3/org.eclipse.jgit.test/tst/org/eclipse/jgit/transport/DaemonTest.java start ephemeral-port daemons inside each test, stopAndWait, and prove the port can be reused after cleanup. Disposition: the maintained examples support isolated ephemeral protocol fixtures with explicit teardown; none supports one mutable server/object database shared across parallel workers. This ticket therefore keeps one isolated large guard, uses isolated small real-protocol fixtures for size-independent oracles, and does not adopt shared mutable state.
